tested: 55 fixed regions x 5 model variants = 275 validated region/method runs; same cached matches, original masks and provenance. Nine five-frame scenes plus two eleven-frame scenes.
finding: Reduced-degree affine/similarity models do not improve the overall coverage-error tradeoff. Spatial deletion sensitivity eliminates all large hidden-patch recovery. Neither difficult road recovers.
control_replay: Converged homography controls reproduce previous policy counts exactly. Nonconverged and disconnected geometry is now forced to abstain.
interpretation: Some common large-patch pixels improve, but local errors regress and coverage falls. This is not a reliable recovery gain. Raw RGB error also mixes geometric and exposure error; add geometric/gradient validation before attributing the cause.
next: Use calibrated perspective plane constraints and source-view observability instead of further affine threshold tuning. Continue new-cohort annotation and keep test groups untouched.
